_comment: What a remote fleet may launch in this repository. Read by an OrbitOrc agent out of this
checkout; nothing in this file is code and nothing here is evaluated.
WHAT A FLEET IS FOR HERE. This addon ships a native library per platform, and the thing no single
machine can check is that the same source produces a working addon on every platform it claims.
So the modes below are the load smoke and the harness, run on a real box of each kind, rather than
a session across machines: there is no session to spread.
A GRAPHICAL SESSION MATTERS EVEN HERE. The smoke asserts that a class registers and a property
round-trips, which a headless run covers. Anything that draws does not, and a box with no session
would report success having rendered nothing.
What a job here needs in order to mean anything, relative to the checkout. These are not where a
build lands -- they are what must already be present, and the native library is the one whose
absence ruins a run quietly: every class it registers resolves to nothing, so the project dies at
load or comes up empty and writes a full metrics file of zeros.
Nothing here declares evidence columns, because this project's jobs are pass/fail smokes rather
than measurements. With no declaration the verdict answers `unknown` for every run, which is the
safe direction: unknown is not a pass, and it is never an accusation.
The load smoke: does a project containing nothing else get a working addon? It prints its own
markers and exits non-zero on the first failure, so the exit status is the verdict and the log
says which check went.
No ready marker: this mode finishes on its own rather than coming up and staying up, so there is
nothing to wait for. It is reported as launched and read from its log.

harness._comment: The harness project with a window, for judging anything that draws by eye on a real box.

_comment: Any scene in the checkout, on a box with a display. The path is positional and lands before the
separator, where the engine reads it -- the one thing no other mode can name. The agent
validates the path against its own checkout before launching: it may name a file inside the
tree and must not become a path out of it.
